prompt:
Create one subject-only illustration for a premium commercial packaging-engineering thumbnail, rendered as a photorealistic high-end 3D product scene. The result should feel like a carefully art-directed commercial studio render, with convincing physical geometry, believable scale, crisp but natural edges, real depth, and physically grounded lighting.

Render every relevant material with recognizable surface detail: corrugated cardboard should show fine paper fibre, subtle flute structure at cut edges, folds, seams, and realistic wear; wood should show natural grain and end grain; plastic should have credible thickness, translucency or restrained gloss; painted metal should show a controlled finish. Use only materials relevant to the requested objects. Avoid smooth generic placeholder surfaces.

Match the owner-approved KolliLabs thumbnail board: sophisticated near-black and deep-teal studio atmosphere, restrained teal edge light, soft directional key light, realistic contact shadows, subtle grounded reflections, and premium commercial depth. Keep the scene physically coherent in scale and perspective; use the specified three-quarter or isometric-like camera rather than a wide-angle or mixed-perspective look.

Composition: keep all meaningful subject matter in the right half of a 16:9 frame and preserve the entire left 46 percent as calm, dark negative space for the deterministic card layout. Use one clear subject scene, a strong silhouette, uncluttered negative space, and a scale that remains legible at the small blog-card size. Blend the subject cleanly with the specified background strategy.

Do not use flat illustration, cartoon rendering, clip art, generic infographic styling, diagrammatic icons, decorative particles or unnecessary set dressing. Do not add extra objects that do not explain the subject. The final card renderer adds the background, typography, logo, and layout. Generate no text, letters, numbers, symbols, labels, logos, screens, watermarks, people, charts, UI fragments, or branding. Do not imply that an editorial illustration is an exact solver output.

Scene-family direction: Two clearly separated physical subjects with matching scale and one calm visual distinction; never use interface screenshots.
Article-specific subject: two side-by-side palletized loads of corrugated shipping cases with visibly different case proportions but matching presentation, each on a natural timber pallet; conceptual comparison only, no exact counted cartons or precise packing pattern
Allowed physical subjects: corrugated_box, pallet
Camera: three-quarter commercial product-studio view, slightly above the two loads, with matching scale and perspective
Materials: natural kraft corrugated cardboard with fine paper fibre, clear folded flaps, scored edges and realistic seams; timber pallet with subtle wood grain and end grain; restrained neutral details; no printed markings
Lighting: premium soft key light from upper left, restrained teal rim light, warm cardboard highlights, convincing contact shadows at carton-to-carton, carton-to-pallet and pallet-to-floor, subtle grounded floor reflection
Blending strategy: transparent_alpha
Additional exclusions: text, logos, people, screenshots, watermarks, visible exact carton counts, precise solver layout, printed labels or symbols, charts or infographic graphics, unnecessary props or clutter
rollback_target: Existing published article thumbnail/front matter remain unchanged.
